title: route degradation fingerprint and io-mode latency breakdown
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a diagnostic dashboard and associated panels that surface per-model and per-route latency fingerprints with explicit breakdowns for streaming vs non-streaming IO paths. The goal is to make it fast to answer: which routes and model versions are regressing, are regressions specific to streaming or sync mode, and what subsystem (runtime, KV cache, batching, network) is the dominant contributor. This ticket covers the dashboard design, the queries/metrics required from telemetry pipelines, trace hook additions to the serving runtime for finer-grained spans, and runbook/alert definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Grafana dashboard deployed to staging containing: per-route small-multiples for p50/p95/p99 with side-by-side streaming vs non-streaming panels
Waterfall decomposition panel that attributes latency to components: routing, deserialization, model-inference, KV cache, batching latency, network egress
Trace link column that opens the sampling trace for any selected route/interval
Metrics pipeline updated so each request metric includes tags: route, model_version, io_mode (streaming|sync), batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit
Alert rule granting a signal when p95 for a route crosses baseline + 3*sigma for 30m with customer_impact=high label
Documentation (dashboard README) describing how to interpret degradation fingerprints and next-step mitigations
tasks: Add io_mode and route tags to request-level histogram metrics (runtime PR) - ENG-52110
Instrument new fine-grained spans in runtime: request_dispatch, kv_cache.fetch, batch_manager.coalesce, kernel_exec - create PR and link traces
Update FluentBit/Logpipeline to preserve route/model tags and forward to metrics cluster
Build Grafana panels: small-multiples p50/p95/p99, waterfall decomposition, scatterplot of latency vs batch_size, error-rate overlay
Create alerts and playbook entries in PagerDuty runbook for route regressions
QA with canary traffic and verify trace links open to Jaeger with correct span tags

notes: Design decisions: prefer histograms for latency (not summaries) to allow aggregation by route/model in ClickHouse. Use 50ms bins up to 10s with exponential tail for heavy tails.
Trade-offs: Increasing tracing sample rate for p99 visibility will increase cost; we will gate to 1% overall and provide on-demand 100% sampling for single-route investigations.
Review feedback from runtime: ensure adding span boundaries is low-overhead and respects fast-path for cache hits; avoid allocations in hot path.
Operational runbook fragment: on p95 spike, check KV cache hit rate panel, check batch_size distribution, open trace for top-10 slow requests, correlate with deployments in the last 60m.
